title: at/on/in (time)
subtitle: at 5 o'clock / on Friday / in June
summary: Learn which preposition of time to use: at for clock times, on for days and dates, in for longer periods.

lesson.heading: at, on and in
lesson.text: We use **at** for the time of day, **on** for days and dates, and **in** for longer periods such as months, years and seasons.

lesson.heading: Expressions with at
lesson.text: We say **at the moment / at present** (= now), **at the same time**, **at the weekend(s)** and **at Christmas** (but *on Christmas Day*). We also say **at night** for nights in general, but **in the night** for one particular night.

examples.text: Can we talk later? I'm busy **at the moment**.
Kate and I arrived **at the same time**.
Will you be here **at the weekend**?
examples.note: or ... on the weekend in American English

examples.text: Do you give each other presents **at Christmas**?
I don't like working **at night**. But I was woken up by a noise **in the night**.

lesson.heading: in the morning or on Friday morning?

right.label: on + a day + morning / afternoon / evening

lesson.heading: No preposition before last / next / this / every
lesson.text: We do not use at/on/in before **last**, **next**, **this** or **every**. We also often leave out **on** before the names of days.

examples.note: or I don't work Monday mornings.

lesson.heading: in a few minutes
lesson.text: We say that something will happen **in a few minutes / in six months** etc., meaning 'from now'. We also use **in ...** to say how long it takes to do something.

examples.text: The train will be leaving **in a few minutes**.
Andy has gone away. He'll be back **in a week**.
I learnt to drive **in four weeks**.
examples.note: = it took me four weeks to learn

lesson.text: Think of the size of the time: a point in the day takes *at*, a whole day takes *on*, anything longer takes *in*.

exercises.prompt: I've been invited to a wedding ___ 14 February.
Amy's birthday is ___ May, but I don't know which date.
Jonathan is 63. He'll be retiring from his job ___ two years.
exercises.explanation: in two years = two years from now.

exercises.prompt: Sam isn't here ___ the moment, but he'll be here this afternoon.
exercises.explanation: at the moment is a fixed expression meaning 'now'.

exercises.prompt: It rained very hard ___ the night. Did you hear it?
exercises.explanation: in the night = during one particular night.

exercises.prompt: I don't like the dark. I try to avoid going out ___ night.
exercises.explanation: at night means nights in general; in the night means one particular night.

exercises.prompt: The office is closed ___ Wednesday afternoons.
exercises.explanation: A day + morning/afternoon/evening takes on: on Wednesday afternoons.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition of time goes with each expression?
Match each sentence with the time expression that completes it.

pairs.left: Neil Armstrong was the first man to walk on the moon
Jazz became popular in the United States
Ben is a very fast runner. He can run 100 metres
If the sky is clear, you can see the stars
After working hard during the day, I like to relax

exercises.statement: I'll see you on next Friday.
exercises.explanation: I'll see you next Friday. We do not use at/on/in before last, next, this or every.

exercises.statement: We were ill in the same time.
exercises.explanation: We were ill at the same time. at the same time is a fixed expression.
Full dates take on: on 10 May 1993.
